guide.summary: English 'can' and 'will' split three ways. 会 is know-how you learned, and also 'will' for a prediction. 能 is being able in practice: the situation, your body or your capacity lets it happen, often with an amount. 可以 is 'it is allowed' or 'that option is open'. Ask which meaning of 'can' you intend: learned it, able to right now, or allowed to.

subs.label: 会: learned skill
subs.focus: Someone has or has not learned how to do something (language, driving, swimming, cooking), no amount, no circumstance: choose 会 / 不会. Classic error: 可以 or 能 for 'know how to'. Add 学过, 没学过 or 从小 so that 能 is not also acceptable.

subs.label: 会: prediction 'will'
subs.focus: A prediction of what will or will not happen (weather, consequence, reaction, 如果 ...): choose 会 / 不会, not 能 or 可以. Classic errors: 明天可以下雨, and 不能 meant as 'won't'. The cue must be an unmistakable prediction, not ability or permission.

subs.label: 会 ... 的: assurance
subs.focus: A promise or reassurance with 会 ... 的 (我会给你打电话的, 他不会忘的). Decide that the modal is 会 (not 能 / 可以), that 的 closes the sentence, and that no 了 is added. Classic errors: 的 placed right after 会, or 会 dropped while 的 is kept.

subs.label: 能: able under the circumstances
subs.focus: The skill is assumed; the situation, time, health or equipment decides whether it is possible now: choose 能 / 不能, not 会 / 不会. Classic error: 我喝酒了，不会开车. Include recovered ability (病好了，能上班了) and 会 ... 但是今天不能. The sentence must state the circumstance.

subs.label: 能 + amount reached
subs.focus: Ability measured by an amount, distance, speed or duration (一顿能吃三碗, 一分钟能打一百个字, 能游一千米): choose 能, not 会 or 可以. Classic error: 他会吃三碗米饭 for 'he can eat three bowls'. Every item needs an explicit number and measure after the verb.

subs.label: 可以: allowed / an open option
subs.focus: Permission (这儿可以拍照) and offering an option (你可以坐地铁去): choose 可以 over 会. Classic error: 我会用你的手机吗 for 'may I?'. 能 is also correct for permission, so never offer 能 as a wrong option there; only in a 'you could ...' suggestion is 可以 the sole natural choice.

subs.label: 不会 / 不能 / 不可以, answering 'may I?'
subs.focus: Pick the negative: 不会 = not learned / won't happen; 不能 = unable or not allowed; 不可以 = not allowed only. Classic errors: 我明天不可以来 for 'can't make it', 不会 for a prohibition. Answers to 可以 ... 吗: 可以 / 行, or 不行 / 不能. Never contrast 不能 with 不可以 in a prohibition.

subs.label: 很会 / 很能
subs.focus: After 很 / 真 / 挺 / 特别: 很会 + verb = skilful (很会做饭, 很会说话); 很能 + verb = large capacity (很能吃, 很能睡). Choose 会 or 能 from the meaning and reject 可以. Classic errors: 很可以做饭, and 很会吃 meant as 'eats a lot'. Context must fix skill versus amount.

rules.rule: For something you learned how to do, use 会. The negative 不会 means you never learned it.

examples.py: wǒ huì kāi chē
examples.en: I can drive. (I know how)

examples.py: tā huì shuō yī diǎn r zhōng wén
examples.en: She can speak a little Chinese.

examples.py: wǒ méi xué guò bù huì yóu yǒng
examples.en: I never learned, so I can't swim.

examples.py: nǐ huì bù huì yòng kuài zi
examples.en: Do you know how to use chopsticks?

rules.note: In everyday speech 能 also turns up with languages (你能说中文吗？ 'are you able to speak Chinese?'), but for plain know-how 会 is the standard choice and the one to produce. 可以 never means 'know how to'.

rules.rule: For a prediction, 'will' or 'is likely to', use 会; 'won't' is 不会. This 会 has nothing to do with skill.

examples.py: míng tiān huì xià yǔ
examples.en: It will rain tomorrow.

examples.py: chuān zhè me shǎo nǐ huì gǎn mào
examples.en: Dressed that lightly, you'll catch a cold.

examples.py: bié dān xīn tā bù huì shēng qì
examples.en: Don't worry, he won't be angry.

examples.zh: 如果你不去，她会很难过。
examples.py: rú guǒ nǐ bù qù tā huì hěn nán guò
examples.en: If you don't go, she'll be very upset.

rules.note: 会 predicts; it does not announce a plan. For 'I'm going to ...' as a decision, Chinese prefers 要 or 打算. 可以 cannot predict, and 不能 does not mean 'won't'.

rules.rule: To promise or reassure, wrap the prediction in 会 ... 的. 的 sits at the very end and no 了 is added.
rules.pattern: Subject + (一定) + (不) + 会 + Verb + (Object) + 的

examples.py: wǒ huì gěi nǐ dǎ diàn huà de
examples.en: I will call you. (I promise)

examples.py: fàng xīn ba tā yī dìng huì lái de
examples.en: Relax, he will definitely come.

examples.py: wǒ bù huì wàng jì nǐ de
examples.en: I won't forget you.

rules.note: The 的 is optional: without it the sentence is a plain prediction, with it the speaker sounds sure and reassuring. It is not the past-tense 是 ... 的.

rules.rule: When the question is whether the situation, your time or your body lets you do it, use 能. 不能 here means 'cannot manage to'.

examples.py: wǒ jīn tiān yǒu shì bù néng qù
examples.en: I'm busy today, so I can't go.

examples.py: nǐ míng tiān néng lái ma
examples.en: Can you come tomorrow?

examples.py: wǒ hē jiǔ le bù néng kāi chē
examples.en: I've been drinking, so I can't drive.

rules.note: 不会 in these sentences would say something else: 我今天不会去 means 'I won't go today' (a prediction), and 不会开车 means 'never learned to drive'.

rules.rule: You have the skill (会) but whether you can use it on this occasion, or again after getting better, is 能.

examples.py: tā de tuǐ hǎo le néng zǒu lù le
examples.en: His leg is better; he can walk again.

examples.zh: 我会游泳，但是今天感冒了，不能游。
examples.py: wǒ huì yóu yǒng dàn shì jīn tiān gǎn mào le bù néng yóu
examples.en: I can swim, but I have a cold today, so I can't.

examples.zh: 她病好了，明天能上班了。
examples.py: tā bìng hǎo le míng tiān néng shàng bān le
examples.en: She has recovered and can go to work tomorrow.

rules.note: 孩子会走路了 is correct for a baby who has just learned to walk: learned for the first time is 会, got the ability back is 能.

rules.rule: If the ability is measured by an amount, a distance, a speed or a length of time, use 能, even for a learned skill.
rules.pattern: Subject + (time span) + 能 + Verb + number + measure + (Object)

examples.py: tā yī dùn néng chī sān wǎn mǐ fàn
examples.en: He can eat three bowls of rice in one meal.

examples.zh: 她一分钟能打一百个字。
examples.py: tā yī fēn zhōng néng dǎ yī bǎi gè zì
examples.en: She can type a hundred characters a minute.

examples.py: wǒ néng yóu yī qiān mǐ
examples.en: I can swim a thousand metres.

rules.note: 会 says only that the skill exists (我会游泳); how much of it you can manage is 能. 他会吃三碗 would be heard as a prediction, 'he will eat three bowls'.

rules.rule: For 'it is allowed' or 'may I?', use 可以. Never use 会 for permission.

examples.py: wǒ kě yǐ jìn lái ma
examples.en: May I come in?

examples.py: zhè r kě yǐ pāi zhào
examples.en: You may take photos here.

examples.py: nǐ kě yǐ yòng wǒ de shǒu jī
examples.en: You can use my phone.

rules.note: 能 is just as common in permission questions (我能进来吗？) and in rules. Between 能 and 可以 for permission there is no wrong choice; the real error is 会.

rules.rule: To offer an option or say something is feasible ('you could ...', 'one way is ...'), use 可以.

examples.py: nǐ kě yǐ zuò dì tiě qù
examples.en: You could go by subway.

examples.zh: 不想做饭的话，我们可以出去吃。
examples.py: bù xiǎng zuò fàn de huà wǒ men kě yǐ chū qù chī
examples.en: If you don't feel like cooking, we could eat out.

examples.py: yǒu wèn tí kě yǐ wèn lǎo shī
examples.en: If you have questions, you can ask the teacher.

rules.note: The negative of this 'could' is not 不可以. 'It can't be done that way' is 不能 or a potential complement such as 去不了.

rules.rule: Three different 'cannot's: 不会 = haven't learned, or won't happen; 不能 = unable, or not allowed; 不可以 = not allowed, and only that.
rules.pattern: Subject + 不会 / 不能 / 不可以 + Verb

examples.py: wǒ míng tiān bù néng lái
examples.en: I can't come tomorrow.

examples.py: zhè r bù néng chōu yān
examples.en: You can't smoke here.

examples.zh: 上课的时候不可以玩手机。
examples.py: shàng kè de shí hou bù kě yǐ wán shǒu jī
examples.en: You may not play on your phone in class.

examples.py: wǒ bù huì zuò fàn
examples.en: I can't cook. (never learned)

rules.note: For a prohibition 不能 and 不可以 are both correct; 不可以 sounds a little more like a rule being laid down. For 'unable', only 不能 works: 我明天不可以来 would mean someone forbids you to come.

rules.rule: Answering 可以 ... 吗 / 能 ... 吗: yes is 可以 or 行; no is normally 不行 or 不能, usually followed by a reason.

examples.py: bù xíng zhè r yǒu rén
examples.en: No (you can't sit here), someone is sitting here.

examples.py: duì bu qǐ xiàn zài bù néng jìn qù
examples.en: Sorry, you can't go in right now.

examples.py: kě yǐ nǐ yòng ba
examples.en: Sure, go ahead and use it.

rules.note: 不可以 as a short answer is grammatical but blunt, the way a parent or a sign speaks. 不会 is never an answer to a request for permission.

rules.rule: 很会 + verb means 'really good at' (skill); 很能 + verb means 'can do a great deal of' (capacity). 可以 does not take 很 in this way.
rules.pattern: Subject + 很 / 真 / 特别 + 会 / 能 + Verb

examples.py: tā hěn huì zuò fàn
examples.en: She is really good at cooking.

examples.zh: 他很会说话，大家都喜欢他。
examples.py: tā hěn huì shuō huà dà jiā dōu xǐ huan tā
examples.en: He is good with words; everybody likes him.

examples.py: wǒ dì di hěn néng chī
examples.en: My little brother can really eat.

examples.zh: 这个孩子真能睡，睡了十二个小时。
examples.py: zhè ge hái zi zhēn néng shuì shuì le shí èr gè xiǎo shí
examples.en: This kid can really sleep; he slept twelve hours.

rules.note: 很会吃 exists too but means 'knows good food', not 'eats a lot'. 很能说 means 'talks a lot', 很会说 means 'speaks cleverly'.

right.py: wǒ xué guò wǒ huì yóu yǒng

contrasts.why: Know-how you learned is 会. 可以游泳 says swimming is allowed or is an option, not that you know how.
A prediction takes 会. 可以 is permission or an open option, and rain needs neither.

right.py: wǒ hē jiǔ le bù néng kāi chē
right.en: I've been drinking, so I can't drive.

contrasts.why: The skill is still there; the circumstance blocks it, so 不能. 不会开车 means you never learned to drive.

right.py: tā yī dùn néng chī sān wǎn mǐ fàn
right.en: He can eat three bowls of rice in one meal.

contrasts.why: A measured amount of ability takes 能. With 会 the sentence is no longer about capacity.

contrasts.wrong: 我明天有考试，不可以来。

right.py: wǒ míng tiān yǒu kǎo shì bù néng lái
right.en: I have an exam tomorrow, so I can't come.

contrasts.why: 'Can't make it' is 不能. 不可以 only means 'not permitted', as if someone had forbidden you to come.

right.zh: 我可以用一下你的笔吗？
right.py: wǒ kě yǐ yòng yī xià nǐ de bǐ ma
right.en: May I use your pen for a moment?

contrasts.why: Asking permission takes 可以 (or 能). 会 would ask whether you know how to use a pen, or whether you will.

right.py: tā de tuǐ hǎo le néng zǒu lù le
right.en: His leg is better; he can walk again.

contrasts.why: An ability you get back after injury or illness is 能. 会走路了 is for a baby who has just learned to walk.

right.en: She is really good at cooking.

contrasts.why: 'Good at' is 很会. 可以 does not combine with 很 to describe skill.

right.py: bié dān xīn wǒ huì bāng nǐ de
right.en: Don't worry, I will help you.

contrasts.why: In the assurance pattern 的 closes the whole sentence; nothing may come between 会 and the verb phrase except adverbs or a coverb phrase.

cheat: Learned how to? 会. Never learned? 不会.
Will it happen? 会 / 不会. Promising? Add 的 at the very end.
A reason in the sentence (busy, ill, drunk, recovered)? 能 / 不能.
A number or measure after the verb? 能.
Allowed, or 'you could ...'? 可以. Permission is never 会.
'Can't make it' is 不能, not 不可以. Saying no to 'may I?': 不行 or 不能.
很会 = skilful; 很能 = a lot; never 很可以 + verb.
